m: Om. I worship Durga, whose splendour is like a mass of lightning, who stands on the shoulder of the lord of beasts, who is terrible, who is attended by maidens whose hands shine with swords and shields, who bears in her hands discus, mace, sword, shield, arrows, bow, noose, and the threatening finger,
whose self is fire, who bears the moon, and who has three eyes. Om. The Goddess said:
Whoever, collected, praises me always with these hymns, of that person I will quiet every affliction. Of this there is no doubt.
And those who tell of the destruction of Madhu and Kaitabha, the slaying of Mahishasura, and likewise the slaying of Shumbha and Nishumbha,
and those who, of one mind, on the eighth, the fourteenth, and the ninth, listen with devotion to this supreme glory of mine,
for them there will be no evil deed, no calamities born of evil deeds, no poverty, and no separation from what is desired.
That person will have no fear from enemies, from a robber, or from a king, nor at any time from weapon, fire, or flood of water.
Therefore this glory of mine should be recited by the collected, and it should always be heard with devotion. It is a great and supreme blessing.
This glory of mine quiets all afflictions arising from a great pestilence, and likewise the three kinds of portent.
Where this is recited properly, every day, in my shrine, I will never leave that place. My presence remains there.
At the offering of a bali, at worship, at the fire rite, and at a great festival, all this glory of mine should be uttered and should be caused to be heard.
I will look with love upon a bali and a worship done knowingly or unknowingly, and likewise upon a fire-offering so made.
At the great worship that is performed in the autumn, and at the yearly one, the devotee who hears this glory of mine there,
freed from every affliction and possessed of wealth and grain, will, by my grace, be such a human being. There is no doubt.
Hearing this glory of mine, and also the auspicious arisings, and the valour in the battles, a person becomes fearless.
Enemies go to destruction, and well-being comes about. The family of the people who hear my glory rejoices.
In a rite of pacification everywhere, and when a bad dream has been seen, and in fierce oppressions by planets, one should hear my glory.
Afflictions grow calm, and the dreadful oppressions of planets. A bad dream seen by people becomes a good dream.
It makes peace for children overcome by the seizers of children. In a break among people it is an excellent maker of friendship.
It is the supreme destroyer of the strength of all who act badly. By the mere recitation it is the destruction of rakshasas, ghosts, and pishachas.
All this glory of mine causes my presence, with animals, flowers, guest-water, and incense, and with excellent scents and lamps,
with the feeding of brahmins, with fire-offerings, with sprinkling-waters day and night, and with other enjoyments and gifts of many kinds, the love which
is made for me over a year is made when this is uttered once, or heard. What is heard takes away sins, and it gives health.
The telling of my births makes a protection from spirits. My deed in the battles, the destruction of the wicked daityas —
when that is heard, fear made by enemies does not arise for people. The praises that were made by you, and those made by the brahmin seers,
and those made by Brahma, let them give an auspicious understanding. In a forest or in a wilderness, surrounded by a forest fire,
or surrounded by robbers in an empty place, or seized by enemies, followed by lions and tigers, or in a forest by wild elephants,
or sentenced by an angry king, condemned, or fallen into bondage, or whirled by the wind, standing in a boat on the great ocean,
or when weapons are falling in a very dreadful battle, or in all terrible afflictions, or even when tormented by pain,
a person who remembers this deed of mine is released from danger. By my power, lions and the rest, robbers, and enemies likewise
flee from afar when one remembers my deed.
The seer said:
Having spoken thus, the blessed Chandika, of fierce valour,
vanished in that very place as all the gods looked on. Those gods too, free of distress, enjoying their shares of the sacrifice,

all took up their own offices as before, their enemies struck down. When Shumbha, enemy of the gods and destroyer of the world, that greatly fierce one of unequalled valour, had been slain by the Goddess in battle,
and when Nishumbha of great valour had been slain, the rest went to the nether world.
Thus the blessed Goddess, though eternal, again and again takes birth, O king, and protects the world.
By her this universe is bewildered, and she herself brings the universe forth. Asked, she gives knowledge; pleased, she gives prosperity.
All this universe is pervaded by her, lord of men, by the great Goddess, Mahakali, whose form is the great pestilence.
She herself, at the time, is the great pestilence. She herself, unborn, becomes creation. She herself, the eternal, at the time makes the continuance of beings.
At the time of worldly life she herself is Lakshmi in the house, the giver of increase. In absence she herself arises as Alakshmi, for destruction.
Praised and fully worshipped with flowers, scents, incense, and the rest, she gives wealth and sons, an understanding set on dharma, and an auspicious course.
